concept.title: How it works
concept.shortdesc: connects iPhones directly to each other with Apple's Multipeer Connectivity framework. There is no server and no relaying through other phones.

section.title: Transport
section.p: Multipeer Connectivity carries all traffic over Bluetooth and peer-to-peer Wi-Fi, using the service type omni-mesh (Bonjour names _omni-mesh._tcp and _omni-mesh._udp). Sessions require Apple's built-in link encryption.
The app declares no background modes, so discovery and connections run only while the app is in the foreground on both phones.

ol.li: Advertise. Each phone advertises at most 24 bytes: a random ID that rotates every 15 minutes (never while a connection is open), the age band, three flags, and a subset of interests.
Connect. Phones running connect automatically, with no tap from either person.

Exchange cards. Connected phones swap signed profile cards: first name, line, age and age band, all interests, scrambled codes for custom interests, and the user ID and public key. The photo and the newest public post and story follow when the owner's settings allow it.
Match. A match exists when both people have said hi. Matches then fetch each other's stories and posts from the author, up to 30 posts and 10 stories.

ul.li: Messages go only directly between the two phones involved. Version never relays through a third phone; a message waiting for its recipient is held for up to 30 days.
An iPhone holds up to 7 Multipeer connections at once. People beyond that limit appear as Someone nearby until their profile arrives.
With more than 50 phones nearby, each new connection is attempted only 5% of the time.
People you haven't matched with are forgotten 30 minutes after they were last seen.
